answer: ALRT is a real time safety alert app. It shows official and community hazard alerts near you on a map and in a list, and it has a Family layer so your circle can share a location snapshot or reach each other in an emergency.

triggers: how do i send an sos
answer: Open SOS and hold the button for 3 seconds. You see who will be alerted, a short countdown, then 12 seconds to undo. SOS alerts your circle, not emergency services.
Your SOS goes to the recipient list you pick on the SOS screen (Everyone by default). You set up those lists ahead of time in Family settings, so you never have to choose during an emergency.
A snapshot shows where you are right now, once. You send it on purpose, and it is deleted after 60 minutes with no history kept. ALRT never tracks you in the background.

triggers: see where they are all the time
answer: ALRT never tracks people in the background. You can send a one-time snapshot (deleted after an hour), start a Journey with updates about every 10 minutes, or send an SOS that lasts an hour.
Go to the Family tab to create a circle and invite people with a link, QR code, or short code. You can have several circles (for example Family, Netball Mums, Site Crew) and switch between them.
Open the circle, scroll to Leaving at the bottom and confirm. This stops SOS both ways and deletes your snapshots for that circle. Your account and other circles stay.

Alerts, the map and emergency guidance are free, with one saved place and 3 Ask ALRT questions a day. ALRT + Individual adds unlimited places and 10 questions a day. Family and Group plans cover check-ins, SOS and Journey for one group.

triggers: how many people can i add
answer: Creating and joining groups is free. For check-ins, SOS and Journey, each person needs ALRT + Individual, or one person covers a group with Family (6), Group 20 or Group 50.
No. ALRT never collects, stores, or shares phone numbers. Your circle reaches you in app, and the only number the app ever dials is your local emergency number.

Open Profile, then the Delete Account option, and type DELETE to confirm. This removes your account and data. If you host a family circle, deleting also dissolves it, so consider transferring it first.
Easy Mode is a simpler layout with large text and a big status button, focused on Map, Alerts, and Family. You can turn it on in your profile settings.

Tap the microphone to talk instead of typing. It is tap to talk only, runs on your device, and the audio is never stored. If you decline the microphone permission the mic is hidden and typing still works.

triggers: why did i get an alert
answer: You are notified for serious official warnings near you (Watch and Act or Emergency level). Community reports and lower level advice show in your list and on the map but do not buzz your phone.
The shape shows who issued it. Triangle: Australian Warning System. Diamond: an official agency. Circle: a community report, unverified. Shield: ALRT. The key is under the map's layers button.

triggers: what does the red alert mean
answer: Colour shows urgency: grey Info, yellow Monitor, orange Action, red Critical. Community reports use their category colour instead. A level word appears only when the agency gives one.
Alerts come from AWS warnings (triangles), official agencies (diamonds) and community reports (circles). Filter sources from the map's layers button and choose categories in Notifications settings.
The Australian Warning System has three levels. Advice: stay informed. Watch and Act: conditions are changing, take action. Emergency Warning: you may be in danger, act immediately.
A community report (a circle) comes from someone nearby and is unverified. Others can confirm or dispute it. Treat it as a heads-up and check official alerts. Post one from the ALRT button.

triggers: who do i call in an emergency
answer: If you are in danger, call your local emergency number now. ALRT is a helper, it does not contact emergency services for you.
